clue.text: People putting on plays including grand shocks

indicators.note: including means one piece holds another within it

parts.note: those who stage plays are stagers
G is the standard abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A theatre company stages productions that hold some grand, startling moments.
explanation.definitionFit: The staggers are a nervous disease of horses, and loosely a fit of reeling, so shocks that make one totter fits.

clue.text: Food baked brown, the first thing to open?

parts.note: tan is a light brown
a door is a thing to be opened
I is the Roman numeral one, the first

explanation.surface: Browned food straight from the oven, the first thing you open.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori dishes are cooked in a tandoor, a clay oven, so the food is baked.

clue.text: Rubbish ravenously eaten — I approve

parts.note: gobbled means eaten greedily
the ego is the I, the self
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: Someone wolfs down junk food and gives it the thumbs up.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobbledegook is meaningless jargon, nonsense talk or rubbish.

clue.text: Former adversary deprived of work, a symbol of power

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: deprived of means the next piece is taken away

parts.note: an opponent is an adversary
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An old rival out of a job becomes a sign of power.
explanation.definitionFit: In maths an exponent is the small raised number giving the power to which a quantity is raised.

clue.text: Show horror as southern half of Yorkshire town wiped out

indicators.note: half of keeps one half of the word's letters
wiped out says the other half of the town's name is erased

parts.note: Huddersfield is a town in West Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Horror as the south of a Yorkshire town is destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' with 'wiped out' keeps the first six of the twelve letters, HUDDER, erasing SFIELD.
explanation.definitionFit: To shudder is to tremble with fear or revulsion, a physical display of horror.

clue.text: Distress as inspector for example crosses motorway

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: crosses means one piece goes over the other, holding it within

parts.note: say means for example
M is for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A police inspector is upset while driving across the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is consternation, a feeling of distress or alarm.

clue.text: Young woman shorn of resistance finally consented: don't do this to Lily!

indicators.note: shorn of means cut free of, so the next piece is taken away

parts.note: a girl is a young woman
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A young woman finally agreed to something, with an aside about the lily.
explanation.walkthrough: To gild the lily is to spoil something already beautiful by over-decorating it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom gild the lily warns against needless adornment, so this is the thing not to do.

clue.text: Awful about death — they hang

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: pants is British slang for awful
an end is a death

explanation.surface: A grim remark that death is terrible, as the condemned hang.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendants are ornaments that hang from a chain or a ceiling.

clue.text: Very fine inhaler I misused

indicators.note: misused means the letters are put to a wrong use, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An asthmatic admits to using their inhaler wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline crack or margin is one as thin as a hair, so extremely slender or fine.

clue.text: Handle blow, retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a bonk is a blow on the head

explanation.surface: An order to grab a weapon and strike, then fall back.
explanation.definitionFit: A knob is a rounded handle on a door or drawer.

clue.text: Look into organised group intending to be obstructive

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a body is an organised group of people
lo is an old word for look
minded to do something means intending to do it

explanation.surface: Someone looks into a well-organised group that seems set on being awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bloody-minded means being deliberately unhelpful and contrary, which is obstructive behaviour.

clue.text: Given a turn newly on a rota in committee, at first like Pre-Raphaelite painting

indicators.note: newly means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A committee member is given a turn on the rota, an artistic gathering perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pre-Raphaelites aimed for close, detailed truth to nature, a naturalistic style.

clue.text: Following music, look at prominent organ

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: pop is a style of music
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: After a song, someone is told to look at a church's impressive organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the instrument, fitting 'music', but it is a body organ: a popeye is a bulging eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A popeye is an eye that bulges, so a sense organ that stands out.

clue.text: Cleopatra was girly in the extreme in brief fancy panties

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside another
fancy means elaborately made over, so the letters are rearranged
brief means cut short, losing the last letter
in the extreme points to the two end letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cheeky claim that the Egyptian queen wore very skimpy, fancy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' leaves PANTIE, 'fancy' makes EPTIAN of it, and 'in' sets the girl's ends within that.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was queen of Egypt, so she was Egyptian by nationality.

clue.text: Halves of beer to begin with one's put round party

indicators.note: to begin with picks out the opening letter of the word
put round means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: one is I, and one's is I'S, one is

explanation.walkthrough: 'Halves' looks like half pints, but it is a verb: cuts into two.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect something is to cut it into two equal parts, so it halves it.

clue.text: Albatross, for one, is out of sorts

definitions.meaning: in golf an albatross is three strokes under par for a hole
feeling a bit unwell, under one's usual standard

explanation.surface: A seabird is feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: The albatross is a golf score, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling below par means being a little unwell, under one's usual standard.

clue.text: Journalist's announcement to create awe

definitions.meaning: a reporter announcing themselves might say they are from the newspapers: I'm a pressman
to strike someone with admiration and wonder

explanation.surface: A reporter announces they are here to amaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress someone is to fill them with admiration, close to awe.

clue.text: About to open grape juice and the Spanish wine

indicators.note: to open means one piece goes into another, splitting it

parts.note: must is unfermented grape juice
ca is short for circa, about
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A wine-making recipe: grape juice and a Spanish touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscatel is a sweet wine made from muscat grapes.

clue.text: After temperature's dropped, arrange prizes for facing the waves

indicators.note: dropped means a piece of the word is taken away

parts.note: to set things is to arrange them
T is short for temperature
awards are prizes

explanation.surface: Once the heat has gone, someone sets out the prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Seawards means toward the sea, so facing the waves.

clue.text: Pretty girls having twinges after exercising

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercising at school
aches are twinges of pain

explanation.surface: Attractive young women are sore after a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach is old slang for an attractive young woman.

clue.text: What can refresh one's day, coming in mostly sluggish

indicators.note: coming in means one piece enters another
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: leaden means heavy and sluggish
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday, a day

explanation.surface: Something to brighten a dull, sluggish day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' leaves LEADE, which 'coming in' opens for the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a cooling soft drink, the kind of thing that refreshes.

clue.text: It may need clipping again, left wild

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Something growing wild again needs a trim.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnail is a hangnail, a torn bit of skin by a fingernail that wants trimming off.

clue.text: Respectful gesture as second warning may be heard

indicators.note: may be heard means the wordplay is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for second; an alarm is a warning

explanation.surface: A polite greeting that might also sound like a quick warning.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, S ALARM is said exactly like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaam is a low bow with the hand to the forehead, a gesture of respect in the Muslim world.

clue.text: On call, not every girl: certainly no aristocrat

indicators.note: not means the following piece is taken away from the word

parts.note: every means all
lass is a girl

explanation.walkthrough: 'call, not every' is CALL with ALL removed, leaving C.

clue.text: Book presenting facts: not the first time

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the truth is the facts

explanation.surface: A book setting out the facts, but losing the first edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Name: Hilary, for example

definitions.meaning: to give something a word to call it by is to name it
Hilary is the spring session of the year at Oxford University

explanation.surface: A name, with Hilary given as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary is the name of a university term at Oxford, and a term is also a word used to call something.

clue.text: Scheme by one engineer after attack artillery repulsed

the Roman numeral I is one

clue.text: Only Charlie is beginning to make an embarrassing mistake

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the opening letter of the word
